title: Qualitative Poisson convergence for birthday triples

problemStatement.formal: Prove p_no_triple_tendsto: for n_c(d) = floor(c*d^(2/3)), P_no_triple(n_c(d), d) tends to exp(-(c^3)/6) as d tends to infinity.
problemStatement.plain: Remove the remaining Lemma C axiom in BirthdayProblemOQ03OQ01OQ02.lean by proving qualitative Poisson convergence for the no-triple birthday event at the k=3 threshold scale.
whyMatters: Reduces the k=3 birthday asymptotic proof from one axiom to zero axioms.
Turns the existing theorem poisson_approx_birthday3 into a fully proved consequence of finite counting and asymptotic probability.
Provides reusable infrastructure for dependent-indicator Poisson convergence in Lean.

proven: asympThreshold and the k=3 threshold asymptotic theorem are present in the parent file.
lambda_tendsto (Lemma A) and exp_lambda_tendsto (Lemma B) are proved.
poisson_approx_birthday3 is proved from exp_lambda_tendsto and p_no_triple_tendsto.
tripleCount connects the no-triple predicate to a finite counting random variable.
The first-moment identity expectedTripleCount_eq is proved.
Layer 3 includes overlapPattern, bad_count_general_4, bad_count_overlap_two, bad_count_disjoint, p_pair_disjoint, and overlap-pattern bounds.
open: Overlap-one joint count and real-probability wrappers are the next local counting targets if still absent.
Layer 3g second-factorial-moment limit and the final method-of-factorial-moments step remain to close Lemma C.
